# `c.<id>.click()` drives a real platform event, on every target.
#
# Each platform fires the event by the mechanism it already exposes, and none
# of them needs layout or a synthetic pointer:
#
#   gtk4       g_signal_emit_by_name on the widget
#   fyne       the widget's own callback field (what test.Tap calls)
#   html       .click() on the element, through its addEventListener
#   bubbletea  the activating key through Update, with focus set
#
# What they all skip is whether the widget is visible, sensitive and hittable:
# a signal emitted at a hidden button still fires. Catching that needs real
# input at a position, which is a different kind of test.
#
# gtk4 had the scaffolding for this and none of the wiring: gtkEventInvoker was
# declared, emitEventInvokers was written and called, and nothing anywhere
# constructed an invoker, so the slice was always empty. The runtime half
# already shipped -- gtk4rt.Emit is g_signal_emit_by_name, commented "used by
# generated test invokers".
#
# No pointer or key simulation is involved, and no layout: emitting the signal
# runs the real trampoline and Go callback bridge, synchronously. What it does
# not check is that the widget is visible, sensitive and hittable -- a signal
# emitted at a hidden button still fires -- which is a different kind of test.

sngl test --platform gtk4 click.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# fyne invokes the widget's own callback field, which is what a real tap does
# and what fyne's own test.Tap does. The field is declared in fyne.sngl:
# Handler{on="click", field="OnTapped"}.
sngl test --platform fyne click.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# html dispatches on the element itself, so the click runs through the same
# addEventListener the page wired rather than calling the handler behind its
# back. The invoker hangs off the state object a test holds, which is what
# makes `c.incClick()` resolve.
sngl test --platform html click.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# bubbletea has no pointer: a button is activated by pressing a key while it
# holds focus, so the invoker sets focus, sends that key through Update, and
# restores focus. That is the platform's own input path, not a shortcut around
# it -- whatever else Update does with the message happens too.
sngl test --platform bubbletea click.sngl
stdout 'ok'

# The invoker is named for the event a program writes, not the one the platform
# subscribes to. gtk4's button override is `@clicked { click() }`, so by the
# time a handler is promoted it is named "clicked" while a test writes
# `click()`. The pairing is recorded during the substitution that inlines the
# program's block, which is the last point both names exist.
sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --out=out rooted.sngl
grep 'func \(m \*Model\) incClick\(\)' out/model.go
grep 'gtk4rt.Emit\(m.inc, "clicked"\)' out/model.go

# A synthesized id is not something a test can name, so it gets no invoker.
! grep 'func \(m \*Model\) __n' out/model.go

sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=fy rooted.sngl
grep 'func \(m \*Model\) incClick\(\)' fy/model.go
grep 'm.inc.OnTapped\(\)' fy/model.go

# html only emits invokers under test mode -- an ordinary page carries no test
# surface at all.
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=bt rooted.sngl
grep 'func \(m \*Model\) incClick\(\)' bt/model.go
grep 'm.Update\(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyEnter}\)' bt/model.go

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --opt test=true --out=ht rooted.sngl
grep 'state.incClick = \(\) =>' ht/index.html
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=plain rooted.sngl
! grep 'incClick' plain/index.html

-- click.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component counter node {
    var n = 0
    vbox {
        text(value="{n}")
        button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
    }
}

func testIncrement(t Test, c counter) {
    c.inc.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
}

window {
}
-- rooted.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

component counter node {
    var n = 0
    vbox {
        text(value="{n}")
        button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
    }
}

window {
    counter()
}
